title: Logarithm setup reaches its initialized state
statement: Fix a natural number $K_0$, an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to each of four query types and each Boolean string, and a Boolean string $x$. For every natural number $k$, state $S$, and Boolean memory $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, if $S.N=k$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, and $S.Lg+hv(k)\le B$, then the program $A(K_0)$ reaches its initialized search state with input-length counter $0$ and logarithm counter $S.Lg+hv(k)$. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies the guard with register bound $B$ and memory-head position between $0$ and $P$, inclusive; the memory remains $M$ and the head is at $0$ at the endpoint.

Fix a natural number $K_0$, an oracle $O$ assigning a Boolean answer to each of four
query types and each Boolean string, and a Boolean string $x$. For every
$k\in\mathbb{N}$, register state $S$, and integer-indexed Boolean memory $M$, if
$S.N=k$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, and $S.Lg+hv(k)\le B$, then the machine
$A(K_0)$ reaches, from the setup state with logarithm counter $S.Lg+hv(k)$ and
input-length counter set to zero, while every intermediate configuration satisfies the
guard with register bound $B$ and memory-head position between $0$ and $P$. The memory
contents remain $M$ and the head begins at $0$.
